Class ChatSession

java.lang.Object
org.casserole.chat.ChatSession
public class ChatSession extends Object
The ChatSession type is the chat state for one SSH connection. SSH is the secure-shell protocol the client used to connect. The message history lives in Roux. Roux is the store that holds the conversation messages. This object holds the session id, the active flag, the system prompt, and the prompt assembly. A caller appends turns, builds the next prompt, and locks, unlocks, or edits a stored message. A blank system prompt leaves no system message in a new region.

    • moodLine

      private String moodLine
      The moodLine field is the console mood text for this SSH session. The empty value means the next prompt carries the system prompt and the turns, without mood text. The opener, the mood line, and the closer are written at the head of one user turn. A transcript of one user turn, or of no user turns, puts that text on the first user turn. A longer transcript puts a new or updated line on the user turn that is being sent. // @aa-sdd PK-1084 docs/specs/common/formal-plan.spec.md

  • Constructor Details

    • ChatSession

      public ChatSession(String systemPromptText, RouxChatMemory memory)
      The constructor opens a memory-only session and mints a random conversation id. A null system prompt is stored as the empty string. The session starts active, and it is not marked restored. The region id is null. ensureSystemPrompt() writes a non-blank prompt as the first system message. adoptStoredMood() copies a mood line that is already stored.
      Parameters:
      systemPromptText - The system prompt from configuration.
      memory - The Roux chat memory that stores the messages.

    • ChatSession

      private ChatSession(String conversationId, OpenResult open, String systemPromptText, RouxChatMemory memory)
      The constructor stores a disk-backed region. A null system prompt is stored as the empty string. The session starts active. If open is null, the session is not restored, the restored count is zero, and the region id is null. If open reports RESTORED, the session is marked restored. The restored count and the region id come from open when it is present. ensureSystemPrompt() and adoptStoredMood() then run.
      Parameters:
      conversationId - The Roux region id.
      open - The open result, or null.
      systemPromptText - The system prompt from configuration.
      memory - The Roux chat memory that stores the messages.

    • exportToon

      public String exportToon()
      The exportToon method returns the whole Roux region for this SSH session as a TOON table. TOON is the text table form of the stored messages. If the export is null or empty, the method returns messages[0]{r,ts,tok,x}: and a line feed. A session mood writes a user row and an assistant row at the head of that table. The user row is the invitation. The assistant row is the opener and the closer. The rows already in the table stay, including their timestamps.
      Returns:
      The TOON message table, or the empty table line when the region is empty.

    • moodHeaderTable

      private String moodHeaderTable(String toon)
      The moodHeaderTable method writes the mood invitation at the head of a message table. A missing mood line returns the table unchanged. A table that does not parse returns the table unchanged. A table that already opens with this invitation and the directive returns the table unchanged. The two new rows use a timestamp of zero and a token count of zero. The rows after those two stay as they were.
      Parameters:
      toon - The table is the message table.
      Returns:
      The table with the header rows, or the original table when no header is written.

    • reset

      public void reset()
      The reset method is the chat start clear. The method drops the stored turns. The mood pin index returns to zero, and a pending mood move is cleared. A configured system prompt is written again. A blank prompt leaves no system message. The session is marked active.

    • stop

      public void stop()
      The stop method is the chat stop change. The session is marked inactive. The history is kept.

    • clearTurns

      public void clearTurns()
      The clearTurns method is the clear change. The method drops the stored turns. The mood pin index returns to zero, and a pending mood move is cleared. A configured system prompt is written again. A blank prompt leaves no system message. The active flag is not changed.

    • appendUser

      public void appendUser(String text)
      The appendUser method stores one user turn. A null text is stored as the empty string. If a mood line is set, no mood move is pending, and the stored user count equals moodPinOrdinal, the stored text is the mood splice plus the turn. The splice is the opener, the mood line, and the closer written at the head of the turn. Otherwise the turn is stored as given.
      Parameters:
      text - The user turn.

    • appendAssistant

      public void appendAssistant(String text)
      The appendAssistant method stores one assistant turn.
      Parameters:
      text - The assistant turn.

    • replaceTurns

      public boolean replaceTurns(List<String> roles, List<String> texts)
      The replaceTurns method drops the turns, keeps the configured prompt, and stores the supplied rows. If either list is null, or the lists differ in length, the method returns false and changes nothing. The mood line, the held line, the pending move, and the pin index are cleared before the role check. If any role is not user or assistant, the method returns false after those mood fields were cleared. Otherwise clearTurns() runs, each row is appended, and the method returns true. A null text is stored as the empty string. After a successful replace, a user row that carries the invitation adopts that mood when the session mood is empty.
      Parameters:
      roles - The role of each row, which must be user or assistant.
      texts - The text of each row, in the same order and length as roles.
      Returns:
      true when the region was replaced, or false when the lists were rejected.

      public org.springframework.ai.chat.prompt.Prompt buildPrompt(int maxMessages, int maxTokens, String newUserText)
      The buildPrompt method builds a prompt with a message cap and a token cap. A maxTokens value of 0 means the window is not limited by tokens. The managed-token allowance is 0, so the sink path is not requested. The lock count is not applied.

    • buildPrompt

      public org.springframework.ai.chat.prompt.Prompt buildPrompt(int maxMessages, int maxTokens, int managedTokens, int headCount, String newUserText)
      The buildPrompt method builds a prompt with a message cap, a token cap, a sink allowance, and a lock count. A maxTokens value of 0 means the window is not limited by tokens. A managedTokens value of 0 uses the message window instead of the sink. A positive allowance asks the memory for a sink cut before the window is used. The lock count is applied before the messages are chosen.
      Parameters:
      maxMessages - The cap on non-system history.
      maxTokens - The token cap, or 0 when the cap is unlimited.
      managedTokens - The sink allowance, or 0 to use the message window.
      headCount - How many non-system turns may lock.
      newUserText - The live user line, which is not stored yet.
      Returns:
      The assembled prompt.

    • assemblePrompt

      private org.springframework.ai.chat.prompt.Prompt assemblePrompt(int maxMessages, int maxTokens, int managedTokens, boolean applyCount, int headCount, String newUserText)
      The assemblePrompt method builds the prompt messages and appends the live user line. A null live line is treated as empty. If applyCount is true, the lock count is applied first. If a mood move is pending, a mood line is set, and more than one user turn is stored, the stored mood rows and splices are removed, the pin moves to the current user count, and the live line is appended already spliced. If a mood line is set and the chosen messages contain a system mood marker but no spliced user turn, the live line is appended and MoodDesk rewrites the mood lines. The system prompt text is passed into that rewrite only when the configured prompt is non-blank. If a mood line is set and neither of those branches ran, splicePinCopy(List) updates the pinned copy and the live line is spliced only when the stored user count equals the pin index. If no mood line is set, the live line is appended as given.
      Parameters:
      maxMessages - The cap on non-system history.
      maxTokens - The token cap.
      managedTokens - The sink allowance.
      applyCount - true when the lock count is applied before the messages are chosen.
      headCount - The configured lock count.
      newUserText - The live user line.
      Returns:
      The assembled prompt.

    • windowOrSink

      private List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> windowOrSink(int maxMessages, int maxTokens, int managedTokens, String live)
      The windowOrSink method chooses the stored turns that go into the prompt. The live line is not included. The over-allowance flag is cleared first. If managedTokens is positive, the live line is counted with a heuristic token counter and the memory is asked for a sink cut. If that cut is present, the over-allowance flag follows the cut and the method returns the sink messages. If the allowance is not positive, or the cut is absent, the method returns the message window for the caps.
      Parameters:
      maxMessages - The cap on non-system history.
      maxTokens - The token cap.
      managedTokens - The sink allowance.
      live - The unsent line, used only to count tokens.
      Returns:
      The stored turns, without the live line.

    • seatMood

      static void seatMood(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> messages, String moodLine)
      The seatMood method inserts a console mood after the first system line. A null message list returns without a change. A null or blank line, after MoodDesk.normalize(String), returns without a change. MoodDesk rewrites the list. A list that already holds this line between the opener and the closer is left as it is. The rewritten messages replace the contents of messages.
      Parameters:
      messages - The prompt, with the newest user turn already appended.
      moodLine - The saved mood, or null.

    • unseatMood

      static void unseatMood(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> messages)
      The unseatMood method removes every stored mood group from a prompt. A null list returns without a change. A system prompt ahead of the mood group stays. A leading mood group with no system prompt is removed together with its closer. The rewritten messages replace the contents of messages.
      Parameters:
      messages - The prompt to rewrite.

    • porchRules

      public static String porchRules(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> messages)
      The porchRules method returns the mood rules text for a pool session. The rules are the opener, the constructed mood, and the closer. That group sits after a system prompt when a system prompt is present. The group sits at the head when the prompt is blank. The system prompt is not included in the returned text. An absent mood group returns empty text.
      Parameters:
      messages - The prompt or the stored region.
      Returns:
      The rules text, or the empty string.

    • setMoodLine

      public void setMoodLine(String line)
      The setMoodLine method stores or clears the console mood in this Roux region. The line is normalized first. If the normalized line equals the current mood line, including both being absent, the method returns. A null normalized line removes the splice from stored user turns, keeps the previous line in moodHeld, and clears the pending move. If there was no current line and the normalized line equals the held line, that line is restored and the splice is written onto the pin when at least one user turn exists. A different new line is stored as both the current line and the held line. If more than one user turn is already stored, the move is left pending and the transcript is not rewritten yet. Otherwise the pin returns to zero, stored system mood rows are dropped, and the splice is written onto the pin. The turns stay.
      Parameters:
      line - The mood string, or null to clear it.

    • adoptStoredMood

      private void adoptStoredMood()
      The adoptStoredMood method copies a stored splice into moodLine. If moodLine is already set, the method returns. A region with no splice leaves the field empty. The transcript is not rewritten. The pin index becomes the zero-based user-turn index whose head matches the adopted line.

      private int countStoredUsers()
      The countStoredUsers method counts stored user turns. A null history returns zero.
      Returns:
      The number of stored user turns.

      private static boolean sameText(String left, String right)
      The sameText method compares two mood lines. Both null values are equal. A null value is not equal to a non-null value.

      left - One line.
      right - The other line.

      true when both are absent or both are equal.

    • dropSystemMoodRows

      private void dropSystemMoodRows()
      The dropSystemMoodRows method removes a stored system mood group. The turns stay. The spliced user turn is written by a later call. The system prompt text is passed in only when the configured prompt is non-blank.

    • stripStoredSplice

      private void stripStoredSplice()
      The stripStoredSplice method removes the mood splice from every stored user turn. A null history returns without a change. A user turn whose head has a mood line is replaced with the unspliced text. If no turn changes, the transcript is not rewritten.

    • writeSpliceOntoPin

      private void writeSpliceOntoPin()
      The writeSpliceOntoPin method writes the current mood line onto the pinned user turn. If no mood line is set, or the history is null, the method returns. The user turn at moodPinOrdinal receives the splice. Another user turn that already has a splice loses it. If the pinned turn is missing, the transcript is not rewritten and the next append can write the splice.

    • splicePinCopy

      private void splicePinCopy(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> promptMessages)
      The splicePinCopy method writes the mood splice onto the matching user turn in a prompt copy. The match text is the unspliced text of the stored user turn at moodPinOrdinal. If that stored turn is missing, the method returns. The first prompt message with the same unspliced user text is replaced with the spliced text.
      Parameters:
      promptMessages - A copy of the prompt messages.

    • systemMoodIn

      private static boolean systemMoodIn(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> messages)
      The systemMoodIn method reports whether a system message is a mood marker. A null list returns false. The markers are MoodDesk.OPENER, MoodDesk.CLOSER, and MoodDesk.LEGACY.
      Parameters:
      messages - The prompt messages.
      Returns:
      true when a system opener, closer, or legacy marker is present.

    • spliceIn

      private static boolean spliceIn(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> messages)
      The spliceIn method reports whether a user turn already carries a mood splice. A null list returns false.
      Parameters:
      messages - The prompt messages.
      Returns:
      true when a user turn already has the splice at its head.

    • replaceTranscript

      private void replaceTranscript(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> stored, List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> next)
      The replaceTranscript method replaces the stored messages when they differ. If the memory says a head is designated, the method returns without writing. If sameTranscript(List, List) says the lists already match, the method returns. Otherwise the region is cleared, the replacement is added when it is non-empty, and a checkpoint is written.
      Parameters:
      stored - The current region.
      next - The replacement messages.

    • sameTranscript

      private static boolean sameTranscript(List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> left, List<org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.Message> right)
      The sameTranscript method compares two message lists by type and text. A null list, or lists of different length, returns false. A null message returns false. A null text is compared as the empty string.
      Parameters:
      left - The stored messages.
      right - The composed messages.
      Returns:
      true when every role and every text already match.

    • countByType

      public int countByType(org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.MessageType type)
      The countByType method counts stored messages of one Spring message type. SYSTEM, USER, and ASSISTANT map to the matching Roux role. Any other type returns zero.
      Parameters:
      type - The message type to count.
      Returns:
      The count for that type, or zero when the type is not one of those three.

    • close

      public void close()
      The close method unmaps the Roux region. A disk-backed close keeps the user directory.

    • ensureSystemPrompt

      private void ensureSystemPrompt()
      The ensureSystemPrompt method writes the configured prompt as the first system message on a new region. A blank prompt leaves the system message off. A region that already holds a system message stays as it is.

    • promptSeated

      private boolean promptSeated()
      The promptSeated method reports whether a new region receives a system message. The result is true when the configured prompt is non-null and its trimmed text is not empty.
      Returns:
      true when a new region receives a system message.
